docs.title: ZATCA e-invoicing for your application
docs.text:
fatoority is an open-source toolkit for developers building e-invoicing integrations in Saudi Arabia. Sign invoice XML, validate it locally, generate QR payloads, and connect to ZATCA APIs for Phase 1 and Phase 2 workflows.

Use the Rust library, add it to your application in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Kotlin/Java (including Android), or C/C++, or run the command-line tool from your terminal.

Try it Choose your language View on GitHub

fatoority is an independent project and is not affiliated with ZATCA.

docs.title: What you can build
docs.text:
Task How fatoority helps Create and sign invoices Build invoice data and sign XML for standard and simplified invoices, credit notes, and debit notes. Validate invoice XML Check UBL schemas, local ZATCA business rules, and applicable signature and QR checks before submission. Generate QR payloads Generate base64-encoded invoice QR data or read the payload embedded in signed XML. Generate a certificate signing request Create a signing key and CSR for device onboarding. Hash invoices Compute invoice hashes and prepare invoice request payloads for API submission. Connect to ZATCA Integrate onboarding, compliance checks, reporting, and clearance into your application.

Local validation helps catch problems before submission. It does not establish ZATCA gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See the validation guide for coverage and how to interpret results.

docs.title: Try it: validate an invoice
docs.text: Start with a local XML schema check. You do not need an account, certificate, or API credentials for this example.

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI
docs.text:
With Rust and Cargo installed, run:

cargo install fatoora-cli

You can also download a binary for your platform from GitHub Releases. Extract the archive and put the fatoora executable on your PATH.

docs.title: 2. Download the sample invoice
docs.text: Save sample-invoice.xml in your working folder. It contains demonstration data for this schema check.

docs.title: 3. Run the check
docs.text:
From the folder containing the file:

fatoora validate --invoice sample-invoice.xml

Expected output:

OK

OK means the XML passes the bundled UBL schema check. To run local ZATCA rules and inspect individual findings, follow the invoice validation guide. For more terminal commands, see the CLI guide.

docs.title: Choose your language
docs.text:
Install the package for your application, then follow its examples. The project and most packages are named fatoority; existing API names such as Python's fatoora import and Rust's fatoora_core remain unchanged.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#Kotlin / Java / AndroidC / C++ 
cargo add fatoora-core

Import fatoora_core in your code. Start with invoice signing or browse the Rust API reference.

pip install fatoority

Import fatoora in your code. Follow the Python setup and examples.

npm install fatoority

Use the WebAssembly package in Node.js or a browser. Follow the JavaScript/TypeScript setup and examples, including browser asset setup and API transport requirements.

dotnet add package Fatoority

Use the Fatoora namespace with .NET 8 or later. Follow the C# setup and examples, including supported native platforms.

Install from Maven Central with Gradle or Maven.

Gradle (build.gradle.kts):

repositories { mavenCentral() }
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.4.4")
}

Maven (add inside <dependencies> in pom.xml):

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.fatoority</groupId>
  <artifactId>fatoority</artifactId>
  <version>0.4.4</version>
</dependency>

Import com.fatoora in your code. Follow the Kotlin/Java examples for supported platforms and Android setup. For Android, use com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.4.4 instead of the desktop artifact.

Download the fatoora-ffi-* archive with the native library and C/C++ headers from GitHub Releases.

Follow the C/C++ setup and examples for compilation and linking instructions.

docs.title: Continue your integration
docs.text:
If you are adding invoicing to an application, start with building and signing an invoice, then validate the XML before sending it.

For device onboarding, generate a CSR, then use the ZATCA API client to request credentials and submit invoices. The guides explain the inputs needed at each step.

docs.title: About the project
docs.text:
The core is written in Rust and shared by the CLI and language bindings. The project code is available under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license. Third-party materials retain their upstream terms; see the third-party notices.

See the SDK compatibility notes for the scope of comparison with the official SDK, and benchmarks for measured performance and methodology.

Need help with an integration? Open an issue. To help improve the library or these docs, read the contributing guide.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: Benchmarks compare Fatoority with the official ZATCA SDK on local fixtures. CLI process timings and warm C# API timings measure different workloads.

docs.title: CLI hashing
docs.text:
CLI invoice hashing benchmark results: - bench/cli/results/hash_bench.md

Command Mean [ms] Min [ms] Max [ms] Relative ZATCA SDK 537.8 ± 8.6 522.0 549.1 187.35 ± 12.59 fatoora-cli 2.9 ± 0.2 2.4 3.6 1.00

The actual script for the benchmark is located at bench/cli/hash_bench.sh

Set FATOORA_CLI to the official SDK executable path and optionally FATOORITY_CLI to this project's fatoora executable. The script otherwise uses the local release or debug build for this project.

docs.title: C# / .NET
docs.text:
Measured on Linux x86_64 with an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, .NET SDK 8.0.425, and Release builds on 2026-10-12. Each value is the median milliseconds per warm call across seven batches after 15 warmup calls.

Operation Invoice Official .NET SDK Fatoority Speedup Hash Simplified 2.487 ms 0.176 ms 14.1× Hash Standard 2.851 ms 0.336 ms 8.5× Sign Simplified 13.630 ms 0.875 ms 15.6× Sign Standard 15.423 ms 1.366 ms 11.3× Validate Simplified 265.453 ms 5.940 ms 44.7× Validate Standard 264.568 ms 5.992 ms 44.2×

Both implementations matched expected hashes, and both signing outputs passed official validation. Both validators accepted the same frozen signed documents. The official SDK's external CEN/KSA rules match our pinned rule sources.

These timings include public API costs: XML parsing, credential parsing in the official signing method, and JSON result parsing in our validator. Our signer reuses parsed credentials. They describe these fixtures on this machine; large invoices, concurrency, HTTP, memory use, and other platforms were not measured.

Fresh-process medians, including startup and one simplified-invoice operation:

Operation Official .NET SDK Fatoority Hash 120 ms 50 ms Sign 248 ms 51 ms Validate 1,260 ms 184 ms

See the C# benchmark harness for reproduction commands and the recorded results for raw samples, binary hashes, and measurement details.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Bug reports, documentation fixes, tests, and code improvements are welcome. For a large API or behavior change, open an issue first so the approach can be discussed before implementation.

docs.title: Set up a checkout
docs.text:
Install stable Rust and Git, then run:

git clone https://github.com/mqqz/fatoority.git
cd fatoority
cargo check --workspace --locked

Ordinary builds and tests need neither Java, an installed ZATCA SDK, nor a system XML library. Language-binding work needs additional tools; see binding development.

docs.title: Find the right place
docs.text: Directory Contents fatoora-core/ Invoice model, signing, XML, validation and API client fatoora-cli/ Command-line interface fatoora-ffi/ Shared bridge for language bindings fatoora-derive/ Procedural macros bindings/ Language facades, packages and their tests docs/ Guides and reference pages bench/ and fuzz/ Benchmark harnesses and fuzz targets

docs.title: Make and check a change
docs.text:
Keep changes focused. Add a regression test for a bug, and update the relevant guide or reference when public behavior changes.

Run these checks from the repository root:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
SKIP_ZATCA_LIVE_API=1 cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked -- --skip doc_example_api

The test command skips live ZATCA requests. Local HTTP tests still need loopback networking. Start with the test for the behavior you changed, then run the workspace checks before submitting.

If you changed… Also check… A binding or shared bridge Generation, language tests and installed packages Validation, signing or XML behavior Validation and SDK compatibility tests Documentation The strict documentation build below Performance-sensitive code The relevant harness in bench/

For longer property-test runs, set PROPTEST_CASES=10000 when running the relevant test. Keep minimized regression inputs and failure seeds. See fuzz/README.md for fuzzing instructions.

docs.title: Edit the documentation
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-macros-plugin
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve

On Windows, use executables under .venv\Scripts instead of .venv/bin. The preview prints its local URL. Before submitting, run:

.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/fatoority-docs

Use a temporary output directory suitable for your system. Guides should walk through a task; reference pages should document inputs, results and behavior. Keep language-specific examples and notes inside the appropriate language tab. Check changed links, narrow screens and every tab you edited.

docs.title: Submit a pull request
docs.text:
Explain the problem, the resulting behavior and how you checked it. Include any remaining limitations. CI runs additional platform and package checks; a local pass does not replace those checks.

Follow the code of conduct. Original contributions are licensed under both MIT and Apache-2.0. Identify third-party material and retain its licenses and notices. For security reports, use the security policy.

Release maintainers can follow the release checklist.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are provided for the latest main branch and the most recent published releases.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security issue, please report it privately (i.e. don't open an issue).

  • Contact: open a GitHub Security Advisory or email the maintainer.
  • Include: a clear description, steps to reproduce, affected versions, and any potential impact.

Please do not disclose the issue publicly until it has been addressed.

docs.title: Disclosure Process
docs.text: After receiving a report, we will: - Acknowledge receipt - Investigate and provide an estimated timeline - Release a fix and coordinate public disclosure

docs.title: Validation and compatibility tests
docs.text: Use these checks when changing validation, XML serialization, signing, QR generation or CSR encoding. The compatibility reference documents user-visible coverage, differences and limits; this page covers maintaining the evidence.

docs.title: Run offline checks
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python3 scripts/business_rules.py check
python3 scripts/integrity_validation.py check
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --test sdk_parity
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --lib sdk_canonical_corpus
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --lib invoice::validation

These checks replay frozen evidence without Java or an installed SDK. Cargo may download missing dependencies; add --offline when dependencies are cached. Missing fixtures, changed checksums and unexpected results fail the checks.

docs.title: Add a regression
docs.text:
Define the expected outcome before changing the implementation. Keep a small failing input and test the result, error or report stage that matters. For a business-rule change, retain the assertion site and location as well as the rule code.

Fixture directory under fatoora-core/tests/fixtures/ Purpose sdk-parity/ Frozen signing, hashing, QR, schema and CSR evidence sdk-parity-typed/ Reviewed captures for changed typed-builder output business-rules/ Rule catalog, coverage ledger and SDK observations

Do not regenerate expected output just to make a failing test pass. Inspect the input, executable rule source and original SDK output. Keep intentional compatibility differences explicit. SDK exit status alone is insufficient: a rejected invoice can still produce exit code zero.

For arithmetic changes, retain independently calculated expectations and exercise rounding boundaries. For integrity changes, include tampered inputs and check that rejection is attributed to the expected stage.

docs.title: Compare fresh output with the SDK
docs.text:
This optional step requires the pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8, its dummy test credentials and a JDK with java and javac. Set FATOORA_HOME to the SDK installation. The tools check the SDK pin and use an isolated copy.

python3 scripts/sdk_parity.py verify \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" \
  --output /tmp/fatoora-sdk-verification

The output directory must not exist. Review report.json and its evidence directory. This checks freshly generated output against the recorded layer outcomes; it does not make live gateway requests.

docs.title: Refresh evidence intentionally
docs.text:
For unchanged input cases, capture a candidate:

python3 scripts/sdk_parity.py capture \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" \
  --output /tmp/fatoora-sdk-candidate

For an intentional serializer or input change, first run cargo run -p fatoora-core --locked --example sdk_parity_export -- /tmp/fatoora-sdk-inputs, then pass --inputs /tmp/fatoora-sdk-inputs to capture.

Business-rule and integrity changes use their own capture commands:

python3 scripts/business_rules.py capture --family ksa-prepayment \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/business-rules-candidate
python3 scripts/integrity_validation.py capture \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/integrity-candidate

Choose the mutation family relevant to the change. Use new output directories, inspect the candidate differences and raw logs, then replace only reviewed fixtures. Preserve manifests, hashes, source notices and the rule-coverage ledger. Run the offline checks again after updating evidence. A new SDK version requires an explicit pin and source review.

docs.title: Binding development
docs.text: Use this page when changing the shared bridge or a language package. Installation and application code belong in the binding reference.

docs.title: Change the API once
docs.text:
1. Implement the behavior and its tests in fatoora-core.
  2. Expose it in the appropriate fatoora-ffi/src bridge: crypto.rs, invoice.rs, or api.rs. Shared errors and input conversion live in common.rs.
  3. Regenerate the bindings. Update a handwritten facade when it needs language-specific conversion or resource handling.
  4. Test the affected language and its installed package. Update public examples and reference documentation.

Preserve exact decimals, absent versus empty values, structured errors and ownership on failure. Test consumed objects, returned children after parent disposal, and concurrent close where relevant. Test HTTP behavior against a local server.

docs.title: Generate and verify
docs.text:
Generated files are checked in. Edit the bridge or generator, then regenerate; do not edit generated output directly.

Install the pinned generators once:

cargo install diplomat-tool --version 0.16.1 --locked
python3 scripts/install_dotnet_generator.py
python3 scripts/install_kotlin_generator.py

The installer scripts select the required fork revisions. Then run:

python3 scripts/generate_bindings.py
python3 scripts/generate_bindings.py --check
cargo test -p fatoora-ffi --locked

The combined check covers all generators, including C# and Kotlin. It requires all three installed tools. For work confined to a handwritten language facade, run that package's checks below without regenerating unchanged bridge code.

docs.title: Check the affected package
docs.text:
C and C++PythonJavaScriptC#Kotlin and Java

Install a C11 and C++17 compiler alongside Rust and Python. Run:

python3 scripts/check_native_bindings.py
python3 scripts/check_c_reference.py
python3 scripts/check_c_examples.py

These compile native callers and exercise ownership, errors and examples. The API example's check does not submit an invoice.

The public C facade is generated from the native headers. Change scripts/generate_c_facade.py or scripts/c_facade_runtime.c when adjusting that facade, then run the combined generation check.

Source builds require Python development headers, CMake, a C++20 compiler and Rust. In an activated virtual environment:

python -m pip install "./bindings/python[dev]"
python -m pytest bindings/python/tests
python -m pip wheel --no-deps ./bindings/python -w /tmp/fatoority-wheels

Install the resulting wheel in a fresh environment and run bindings/python/tests/wheel_smoke.py. Keep the source package off PYTHONPATH so the check uses the installed package and its bundled native library.

Add facade regressions for decimal conversion, exceptions, lifetime handling or GIL behavior when those contracts change.

Install Node.js 22+, npm and the Rust WASM target:

rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm ci --prefix bindings/js
python3 scripts/build_js.py
npm run check --prefix bindings/js
node bindings/js/tests/runtime.test.mjs
npx --prefix bindings/js playwright install chromium
node bindings/js/tests/browser.mjs
python3 scripts/check_js_package.py

Use the build script so optimization and artifact-size checks run consistently. The checks cover declarations, runtime behavior, browser loading and an installed npm package.

Install the .NET SDK required by bindings/dotnet, plus Rust and Python. Run:

python3 scripts/generate_dotnet.py --check
python3 scripts/check_dotnet.py

To test an already built NuGet package as well, pass --package-dir dist/dotnet. Keep disposal, optional results, borrowed byte views and error ownership covered by the package tests.

Install the JDK required by bindings/kotlin, plus Rust and Python. Use the checked-in Gradle wrapper:

python3 scripts/generate_kotlin.py --check
python3 scripts/build_kotlin.py
bindings/kotlin/gradlew -p bindings/kotlin test -PnativeDir="$PWD/target/jvm-release"
python3 scripts/check_kotlin.py

The package check uses a fresh Java consumer. Android changes also need the Android build and emulator checks described in the package README. Preserve both language interfaces when changing factories, optional values or exceptions.

docs.title: Before submitting
docs.text: Run the workspace checks, review generated diffs, and test the packaged library rather than only a build-tree import. Include the relevant license and notice files when changing packaging. Platform-specific changes need their platform CI results.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text: This page is for maintainers publishing a release. A version tag starts independent publication workflows for crates.io, PyPI, npm, NuGet, Maven Central and native release assets. Merging a release PR does not publish packages.

docs.title: Prepare the candidate
docs.text:
Create a release/<version> branch. Keep one version across all packages:

Update Files Rust packages and internal dependencies The four crate manifests and root Cargo.lock Python bindings/python/pyproject.toml and bindings/python/uv.lock JavaScript bindings/js/package.json and bindings/js/package-lock.json C# bindings/dotnet/Fatoora.csproj Kotlin and Java bindings/kotlin/build.gradle.kts Independent Rust workspaces fuzz/Cargo.lock and scripts/xsd-compat/Cargo.lock

Avoid unrelated dependency upgrades. Add a curated changelog entry, including migration instructions for changed public contracts. Leave the release date as Unreleased until publication.

docs.title: Validate before tagging
docs.text:
Run the workspace checks, affected binding checks and the following commands. Substitute the intended release tag:

python3 scripts/check_release.py --tag v0.4.4
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked
cargo package --workspace --list
cargo publish --workspace --locked --dry-run

The release checker requires Python 3.11+; workspace publication requires Cargo 1.90+. Package verification can require registry access. Fix failures rather than bypassing verification.

Inspect packages for expected code, schemas, native libraries, headers and licenses. Test installed packages in fresh consumers. Run python3 scripts/check_xml_free_artifacts.py <artifact paths> on the built native archives and wheels. Wait for the candidate's platform and package CI checks, and recheck the final commit after changes.

docs.title: Check publication access
docs.text:
Confirm registry ownership and credentials without printing secret values. Versions must be unused at each destination.

Destination Publication setup crates.io CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN with access to all four crates PyPI Trusted publisher for python.yml and the pypi environment npm NPM_TOKEN with access to fatoority NuGet Trusted publisher for dotnet.yml Maven Central Verified namespace, Central token and signing key

The publication workflows in .github/workflows/ define the registry configuration.

docs.title: Publish and verify
docs.text:
After the release PR is reviewed and merged, tag the exact tested commit. Replace the version and commit below:

git tag -a v0.4.4 TESTED_COMMIT_SHA -m "Release v0.4.4"
git push origin v0.4.4

Check each registry and native release asset independently. Verify installation in fresh consumers and the docs.rs build, then publish the curated release notes and date. An uploaded artifact or one green workflow is not proof that every package was published.

docs.title: Recover a partial release
docs.text:
Keep the tag fixed. Check which versions exist and whether a registry deployment is still pending before retrying. Resume only missing publications from that same commit.

The sequential Cargo publisher can stop on an already-published crate; do not blindly rerun it. npm, NuGet and Central support workflow-specific retries on the existing tag. For Central, inspect the deployment status before uploading another bundle. Published versions are immutable; a code fix needs a new version.

docs.title: SDK compatibility and limits
docs.text: fatoority uses recorded evidence from ZATCA SDK 238-R3.4.8 to check invoice hashes, canonical XML, signatures, QR data, CSR structure and validation outcomes. Running the library requires neither Java nor an SDK installation.

docs.title: What is covered
docs.text:
Area Scope Invoice formats Standard and simplified invoices, credit notes and debit notes Signing and hashing Canonical bytes, invoice digests, signed properties and signature integrity QR Encoded fields and their relationship to invoice and certificate data CSR English/Arabic subjects, environments, encoding and signatures Local validation Bundled UBL schema, 105 CEN assertion sites, 152 Saudi assertion sites and applicable integrity checks

The validation reference explains report stages and outcomes. The schema-only operation checks XSD; the local ZATCA operation runs the wider pipeline. Signature and QR checks are inapplicable to standard documents under this profile.

Compatibility tests are evidence for the cases they cover. They do not establish certificate issuer trust, revocation status or remote invoice acceptance. Some fixtures intentionally contain rejected invoices; do not treat every fixture as a compliant template.

docs.title: Known differences and limitations
docs.text:
Policy Behavior SDK-QR-001 QR generation, signing integrity and SDK-profile validation use PayableAmount (BT-115) for tag 4, including prepayment and payable rounding adjustments. This matches the recorded SDK behavior and the Fatoora Developer Community clarification for SDK 3.3.1 and later. SDK-QR-002 Tag 3 must contain a complete RFC3339 timestamp; a missing offset is interpreted as UTC. Comparison uses instants. Native validation rejects inconsistent offsets, a different day and malformed suffixes accepted by the recorded SDK CLI runs. SDK-QR-003 Tag 5 uses exact XML-decimal equality. Native validation rejects NaN, exponent syntax and distinct values that collapse to the same binary float. Captures also show the SDK accepting 16.0 against invoice VAT 15.00; native validation rejects that mismatch. LOCAL-INTEGRITY-001 Signature algorithms, references and structure are restricted to the supported profile. Duplicate IDs, unbound references and malformed TLV data are rejected. This is a constrained invoice verifier; arbitrary XMLDSig transforms are unsupported.

The signing contract does not authenticate the signing-time field as a trusted timestamp. Keep that distinction when using signature metadata for audit records.

The recorded foreign-currency builder case fails the SDK rule requiring SAR as VAT accounting currency. Choose invoice currency and tax-accounting behavior according to your integration requirements, and inspect the local validation report before submission.

docs.title: Validation resource limits
docs.text:
Resource Limit XML input 8 MiB Element nodes 100,000 Element depth 128 Retained XML data 64 MiB Decimal digits 4,096 Findings 10,000 Finding data 8 MiB

Exceeding a limit produces an execution error, potentially with a partial report. DTD declarations in invoice input are rejected. Pattern evaluation has additional bounded resource use. See error details.

docs.title: Evidence and maintenance
docs.text:
The frozen manifest retains the historical SDK-QR-001 mismatch from its capture; it does not describe current QR generation. Current regression tests require both SDK and Rust QR tag 4 to match PayableAmount.

The frozen corpus records SDK outputs and checksums. The recorded verification report identifies the source and artifacts checked in that run; it is not a verification of every subsequent commit.

Contributors changing these behaviors should follow validation testing.

docs.title: Connect to ZATCA APIs
docs.text: Use the API client to submit invoices and inspect the gateway's response. This walkthrough reports a simplified invoice to the non-production environment and checks whether reporting was accepted. It requires network access and credentials.

docs.title: Choose the operation
docs.text:
Your task Operation Credentials Test an invoice during onboarding Compliance check Compliance credentials Submit a simplified invoice Reporting Production-type credentials for the selected environment Submit a standard invoice Clearance Production-type credentials for the selected environment

A credential's type and its environment are separate. Production-type credentials can target non-production, simulation, or production; the client and credentials must agree. Every example below uses non-production. Changing only the client environment does not convert credentials issued for another environment.

docs.title: Obtain credentials
docs.text:
1. Generate a CSR and private key for the target environment.
  2. Obtain the onboarding one-time password (OTP) through the appropriate ZATCA flow, then submit the CSR to request compliance credentials.
  3. Use those credentials to complete the required invoice compliance checks.
  4. Request production-type credentials for that environment, then retain the returned token and secret for reporting or clearance.

See the credential endpoint reference and ZATCA developer portal for the request fields and environment-specific onboarding requirements. A successful compliance check alone is not reporting or clearance acceptance.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Use your own signed.xml: a simplified invoice signed with the certificate and key associated with your credentials. The offline guide's public test certificate is not a substitute for credentials issued to you.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in the environment of the process running the example. Do not paste credentials into source files. The example reads these names and fails before sending a request if either value is missing.

docs.title: Run the example
docs.text:
Choose your language, then follow its setup and run instructions.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

Install Rust and Cargo, then create a project:

cargo new fatoority-guide
cd fatoority-guide
cargo add fatoora-core

Add the async runtime:

cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread

Save the code below as src/main.rs. Put the input files in the project root and run:

cargo run

Download this example.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

use fatoora_core::api::{CsidCredentials, Production, ZatcaClient};
use fatoora_core::config::{Config, EnvironmentType};
use fatoora_core::invoice::xml::parse::parse_signed_invoice_xml;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let environment = EnvironmentType::NonProduction;
    let token = std::env::var("ZATCA_TOKEN")?;
    let secret = std::env::var("ZATCA_SECRET")?;
    let client = ZatcaClient::new(Config::new(environment))?;
    let credentials = CsidCredentials::<Production>::new(environment, None, token, secret);
    let xml = std::fs::read_to_string("signed.xml")?;
    let invoice = parse_signed_invoice_xml(&xml)?;
    let response = client.report_simplified_invoice(&invoice, &credentials, false, Some("en")).await?;
    response.ensure_accepted()?;
    println!("Invoice reporting accepted");
    Ok(())
}

Install the package in your Python environment:

pip install fatoority

Save the code as api.py beside the input files, then run:

python api.py

Download this example. See Python setup for package details.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread.

from pathlib import Path
import os
from fatoora.api import CsidProduction, ZatcaClient
from fatoora.config import Config, Environment
from fatoora.invoice import parse_signed_invoice_xml

# Use credentials issued for this same environment.
environment = Environment.NON_PRODUCTION
token = os.environ["ZATCA_TOKEN"]
secret = os.environ["ZATCA_SECRET"]
with Config(environment) as config, ZatcaClient(config) as client:
    with CsidProduction.new(environment, token, secret, None) as credentials:
        with parse_signed_invoice_xml(Path("signed.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) as invoice:
            with client.report_simplified_invoice(invoice, credentials, False, "en") as response:
                response.ensure_accepted()
                print("Invoice reporting accepted")

Use Node.js 22 or later. In a new working folder, install the package:

npm install fatoority

Save the code as api.mjs beside the input files, then run:

node api.mjs

Download this example. These examples run in Node.js and can also be adapted to TypeScript. In a browser, replace filesystem reads with your application's file input and configure the WASM asset as described in the browser setup. Keep objects in the WASM instance that created them; do not pass them between workers.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

Browser requests also depend on gateway CORS. Keep private credentials on a trusted server.

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { Config, CsidProduction, SignedInvoice, ZatcaClient } from 'fatoority';

const environment = 0; // Non-production; credentials must match.
const token = process.env.ZATCA_TOKEN;
const secret = process.env.ZATCA_SECRET;
if (!token || !secret) throw new Error('Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET first');
const client = new ZatcaClient(Config.new_(environment));
const credentials = CsidProduction.create(environment, null, token, secret);
const invoice = SignedInvoice.fromXml(readFileSync('signed.xml', 'utf8'));
const response = await client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, false, 'en');
response.ensureAccepted();
console.log('Invoice reporting accepted');

Use the .NET 8 SDK or later. Create a console application:

dotnet new console -n FatoorityGuide
cd FatoorityGuide
dotnet add package Fatoority

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(argc == 1 ? stdout : stderr,
            "Usage: %s signed-invoice.xml\n"
            "Submits a simplified invoice to the non-production gateway.\n", argv[0]);
        return argc == 1 ? 0 : 1;
    }
    const char *token = getenv("ZATCA_TOKEN"), *secret = getenv("ZATCA_SECRET");
    if (!token || !secret) { fputs("Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET first.\n", stderr); return 1; }
    FatooraConfig *config = NULL;
    FatooraSignedInvoice *invoice = NULL;
    FatooraCsidProduction *credentials = NULL;
    FatooraZatcaClient *client = NULL;
    FatooraValidationResponse *response = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_signed_invoice_from_file(argv[1], &invoice, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_config_new(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &config, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_zatca_client_create(config, &client, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_csid_production_create(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, NULL,
        token, secret, &credentials, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_zatca_client_report_simplified_invoice(client, invoice,
        credentials, false, "en", &response, &error));
    /* Receiving a response does not establish acceptance. */
    TRY(fatoora_validation_response_ensure_accepted(response, &error));
    puts("Invoice reporting accepted.");
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (exit_code) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n%s\n", (int)status,
        fatoora_error_message(error), fatoora_error_details_json(error));
    fatoora_validation_response_free(response);
    fatoora_zatca_client_free(client);
    fatoora_csid_production_free(credentials);
    fatoora_signed_invoice_free(invoice);
    fatoora_config_free(config);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return exit_code;
}

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
The example prints Invoice reporting accepted only after checking the reporting outcome. An HTTP 2xx response that decodes successfully does not by itself mean the invoice was accepted.

Outcome What to do Accepted Record the response and retain warnings. For compliance, this means only that the compliance check passed. Rejected Inspect validation messages and correct the invoice before another submission. Unknown Inspect the original status fields; missing, unfamiliar, or contradictory evidence cannot establish acceptance.

Non-2xx responses are errors and retain HTTP status and response details when available. Avoid blind retries when the result of a submission is uncertain.

docs.title: Use clearance for a standard invoice
docs.text:
Choose the clearance operation with a standard invoice and credentials for the same environment. Check the clearance outcome, then retrieve the returned cleared invoice if your workflow needs the gateway document. Save that XML directly.

Acceptance does not guarantee the optional cleared document is present or decodable. Decoding the field establishes UTF-8 text only; it does not parse XML or verify a signature. The clearance reference describes the operation and response accessors.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Missing credential variable Set both named environment variables in the process that runs the example. Authentication or authorization error Check the token, secret, credential type, and environment together. Invoice rejected Read the gateway's validation messages and compare them with local validation. Network error or timeout Check connectivity and the selected endpoint; determine whether a request reached the gateway before retrying. Accepted clearance without usable XML Handle the missing or invalid document explicitly; do not silently substitute the submitted XML.

See the API reference for onboarding, renewal, compliance, reporting, clearance, and complete response contracts.

docs.title: Use the fatoora command-line tool
docs.text: Run invoice tasks from your terminal without writing an application. This guide starts with a local schema check, then shows CSR generation, signing, and QR operations. The executable is named fatoora; the installable crate is fatoora-cli.

docs.title: Install and check the command
docs.text:
Choose one installation method:

  • With Rust and Cargo, run cargo install fatoora-cli.
  • Download the fatoora-cli-* archive for your platform from GitHub Releases. Extract it and add the folder containing fatoora (or fatoora.exe) to your PATH.

Release archives use .tar.gz on Linux/macOS and .zip on Windows. They include license texts and rule notices under licenses/zatca/.

Open a terminal and check the installation:

fatoora --help

You should see the command list. Use fatoora <command> --help for that command's options, for example fatoora sign --help.

docs.title: Validate your first invoice
docs.text:
Save sample-invoice.xml in your working folder, open a terminal there, and run:

fatoora validate --invoice sample-invoice.xml

Expected output:

OK

This checks the bundled UBL schema locally. It does not run the full ZATCA profile or submit the invoice. No account or credentials are needed.

docs.title: Run local ZATCA checks
docs.text:
For a practice report, download invoice.xml and previous-hash.txt. This unsigned sample passes the schema check but can produce signature and QR findings under the full profile. The predecessor file is context for this sample only.

Linux / macOS shellPowerShell 
fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json \
  --previous-invoice-hash "$(cat previous-hash.txt)"

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json `
  --previous-invoice-hash (Get-Content -Raw previous-hash.txt).Trim()

For real invoices, obtain the predecessor hash from trusted invoice history. Read is_valid, is_complete, and the stage findings in the JSON output. A complete local check still does not establish gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See invoice validation for interpreting the report.

Use --evaluated-at with an RFC3339 timestamp only when you need a fixed evaluation time, such as a reproducible historical test. Otherwise the command uses the current clock.

docs.title: Generate a CSR and private key
docs.text:
Download csr.properties for a non-production practice run, then run:

fatoora csr --csr-config csr.properties --generated-csr csr.pem --private-key key.pem --pem

This writes csr.pem and key.pem. Keep the key private. Before onboarding your own device, replace the sample properties using the CSR guide.

--pem selects PEM text; without it, output is base64 DER. Without output-file options, the command writes the CSR and key to standard output.

docs.title: Sign invoice XML
docs.text:
For a local example, download invoice.xml, certificate.pem, and private-key.pem. The certificate and key are public demonstration fixtures, not credentials for your business.

fatoora sign --invoice invoice.xml --cert certificate.pem --key private-key.pem --signed-invoice signed.xml

The command writes signed.xml. Use your own matching certificate and key in an integration. The signing guide explains their origin and the next validation step. Certificate and key formats must match: both PEM, or both DER with --cert-format der --key-format der.

Output-file commands can replace existing files; choose paths appropriate to your workflow.

docs.title: Read or generate QR payloads
docs.text:
To read the payload already embedded in signed.xml:

fatoora qr-read --invoice signed.xml

To generate a payload from an unsigned invoice:

fatoora qr --invoice invoice.xml

qr can also regenerate from signed XML. Add --fail-on-signed when your workflow should reject signed input. Output is base64-encoded text; redirect it to qr.txt if needed. The QR guide explains how to pass it to an image renderer.

docs.title: Compute a hash or prepare a request payload
docs.text:
fatoora generate-hash --invoice invoice.xml

This prints a base64 invoice hash. For signed XML, it prints the signed hash; otherwise it hashes finalized invoice XML.

fatoora invoice-request --invoice signed.xml --api-request request.json

This writes a request payload to request.json. It does not submit it. Continue with the API integration guide to handle credentials and acceptance.

docs.title: Interpret validation exit codes
docs.text:
The default schema command and the ZATCA profile have different exit contracts:

Mode Exit code Meaning Schema check 0 Schema valid; prints OK Schema check 1 Validation or execution failure ZATCA profile 0 Valid, including complete coverage; warnings can remain ZATCA profile 2 Invoice rejected ZATCA profile 3 Execution failure; inspect any partial report ZATCA profile 4 Incomplete coverage Command usage 2 Invalid arguments; read the usage message

Do not interpret code 2 without considering whether arguments were accepted and a validation report was produced.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Command not found Extract the release archive, update PATH, and open a new terminal. Input file not found Run from the input folder or use an absolute path. Certificate/key error Check that the pair matches and both files use the selected format. Incomplete report Supply trusted predecessor context and inspect missing stages.

For a full walkthrough of a specific task, continue with CSR generation, signing, or validation.

docs.title: Generate a ZATCA CSR and private key
docs.text: A certificate signing request (CSR) contains the identity and public key of your invoicing device. Use it during onboarding to request credentials from ZATCA. This walkthrough creates a CSR and its matching private key locally.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Download csr.properties into a working folder. The sample contains demonstration values and targets the non-production environment. You can run it unchanged to learn the workflow.

For your own device, replace the sample values:

Property What to supply csr.common.name Your device or solution common name csr.serial.number The solution serial number in ZATCA's required format csr.organization.identifier Your organization's VAT identifier csr.organization.unit.name The branch or organizational unit csr.organization.name The legal organization name csr.country.name The country code, such as SA csr.invoice.type The invoice-type capability code required for your device csr.location.address The business location csr.industry.business.category The business activity

Use the current field requirements from the ZATCA developer portal when onboarding a real device. The sample values are not a registration for your business. Keep the CSR environment consistent with the API environment you will use next. The examples replace csr.pem and key.pem if those files already exist.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static int write_pem(const char *path, const char *pem) {
    FILE *file = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!file) return 0;
    int written = fputs(pem, file) >= 0;
    return fclose(file) == 0 && written;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s csr.properties\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraCsrProperties *properties = NULL;
    FatooraSigningKey *key = NULL;
    FatooraCsr *csr = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *csr_pem = NULL, *key_pem = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_csr_properties_parse_csr_config_file(argv[1], &properties, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signing_key_generate(&key, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_csr_properties_build(properties, key, FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &csr, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_csr_to_pem(csr, &csr_pem, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signing_key_to_pem(key, &key_pem, &error));
    if (!write_pem("key.pem", key_pem) || !write_pem("csr.pem", csr_pem)) {
        fputs("Unable to write key.pem or csr.pem.\n", stderr);
        goto cleanup;
    }
    puts("Saved csr.pem and key.pem");
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status != FATOORA_OK) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_string_free(key_pem);
    fatoora_string_free(csr_pem);
    fatoora_csr_free(csr);
    fatoora_signing_key_free(key);
    fatoora_csr_properties_free(properties);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return exit_code;
}

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Read a PEM file into a NUL-terminated string. */
static char *read_pem(const char *path) {
    FILE *file = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!file) return NULL;
    char *data = NULL;
    if (fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END)) goto done;
    long size = ftell(file);
    if (size <= 0 || size > 1024 * 1024) goto done;
    rewind(file);
    data = malloc((size_t)size + 1);
    if (!data) goto done;
    if (fread(data, 1, (size_t)size, file) != (size_t)size) {
        free(data);
        data = NULL;
    } else {
        data[size] = '\0';
    }
done:
    fclose(file);
    return data;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s invoice.xml certificate.pem private-key.pem\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    char *cert = read_pem(argv[2]);
    char *key = read_pem(argv[3]);
    if (!cert || !key) {
        fputs("Unable to read certificate or private key PEM.\n", stderr);
        free(cert);
        free(key);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraSigner *signer = NULL;
    FatooraFinalizedInvoice *invoice = NULL;
    FatooraSignedInvoice *signed_invoice = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *xml = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_signer_from_pem(cert, key, &signer, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_finalized_invoice_from_file(argv[1], &invoice, &error));
    /* Signing consumes invoice's inner state; its outer handle still needs free. */
    TRY(fatoora_signer_sign(signer, invoice, &signed_invoice, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signed_invoice_into_xml(signed_invoice, &xml, &error));
    puts(xml);
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (exit_code) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_string_free(xml);
    fatoora_signed_invoice_free(signed_invoice);
    fatoora_finalized_invoice_free(invoice);
    fatoora_signer_free(signer);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    free(cert);
    free(key);
    return exit_code;
}

docs.title: Generate and read ZATCA QR payloads
docs.text: A ZATCA invoice QR code contains a base64-encoded TLV (tag-length-value) payload. fatoority exposes that text so you can store it or pass it to a QR image renderer. This walkthrough reads an existing payload from a signed invoice and saves qr.txt.

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text: The example writes qr.txt, containing the base64-encoded payload. It is text, not a PNG or SVG. Tags 1–5 carry seller and amount data; signing tags are present when supplied by the invoice. The encoded payload must fit the supported size limit.

docs.title: Render a QR image
docs.text:
Read the payload from qr.txt, removing any trailing line break from terminal output. Pass that base64 text directly to your application's QR rendering library. Do not base64-encode the text again. Select the image size and output format for your receipt or invoice layout, then scan the rendered image to confirm it decodes to the same payload.

Image rendering is a separate step; fatoority does not produce an image file here.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check No embedded payload can be read Use signed XML that contains QR data, or create a signed invoice first. Generation reports missing seller fields Supply the seller name and VAT identifier in the invoice. Payload exceeds a length limit Check field byte lengths, including UTF-8 text, and the encoded payload length. QR scanning returns unexpected text Feed the encoded payload directly to the renderer; avoid extra encoding or wrapping.

Next, validate the invoice's QR and signature checks. See the QR reference for payload limits and error types.

docs.title: Validate ZATCA invoice XML
docs.text:
Check an invoice before submission and inspect the results to decide what needs fixing. Choose a schema check for XML structure, or the local ZATCA profile for business rules and applicable integrity checks.

Check What it tells you UBL schema Whether the XML conforms to the bundled invoice schema Local ZATCA profile Business-rule findings, applicable signature/QR checks, and which stages were covered

Neither check establishes ZATCA gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. Building, parsing, or signing an invoice does not automatically run the full local profile.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Save invoice.xml in your working folder. For the local ZATCA check, also save previous-hash.txt. This file supplies the known predecessor context for this demonstration invoice. For real invoices, use the previous invoice's hash from your trusted invoice history; do not copy the current document's claimed predecessor value as independent evidence.

Validate the original XML. Parsing and reserializing it first can change the document being checked. All schemas are bundled; the check does not contact a gateway.

The sample is unsigned: it is useful for a successful schema check and for exploring ZATCA findings. Do not expect its full local report to pass signature checks.

    char *xml = read_xml(argv[1]);
    if (!xml) {
        fputs("Unable to read invoice XML.\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    bool valid = false;
    char *options = NULL, *report = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_config_new(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &config, &error));
    /* Validate original XML; parsing/reserializing would change the input. */
    if (argc == 3) {
        options = read_xml(argv[2]);
        if (!options) { fputs("Unable to read validation options.\n", stderr); goto cleanup; }
        TRY(fatoora_xml_validate_zatca(config, xml, options, &report, &error));
        puts(report);
        /* Parse is_valid/is_complete with your application's JSON parser before accepting.
           Here exit 0 means the report was produced, not that the invoice passed. */
        valid = true;
    } else {
        TRY(fatoora_xml_validate(config, xml, &valid, &error));
        printf("XSD valid: %s\n", valid ? "true" : "false");
    }
cleanup:
    if (status != FATOORA_OK)
        fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    free(options);
    fatoora_string_free(report);
    free(xml);
    fatoora_config_free(config);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return status == FATOORA_OK && valid ? 0 : 1;
}

Run the local ZATCA checks

Save validation-options.json beside the input. It contains predecessor context for the sample only.

./validation invoice.xml validation-options.json

The example prints the JSON report. Exit 0 here means a report was produced; parse is_valid and is_complete with your application's JSON parser before accepting the invoice.

Install the command-line tool with cargo install fatoora-cli, or extract a release binary and add it to your PATH. See the CLI guide for platform setup. Run beside your input files:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml

For local ZATCA rules, use your shell to pass the predecessor hash. In a POSIX shell:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json \
  --previous-invoice-hash "$(cat previous-hash.txt)"

In PowerShell:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json `
  --previous-invoice-hash (Get-Content -Raw previous-hash.txt).Trim()

The schema command prints OK. The ZATCA command prints a report and returns 0 for valid, 2 for rejected, 3 for execution failure, or 4 for incomplete coverage.

docs.title: Interpret the result
docs.text:
A successful schema check prints a success message. It says nothing about business rules or gateway acceptance. A local ZATCA check prints a structured report:

Result How to use it is_valid: true The invoice passes the configured local profile with complete coverage. Keep any warnings. is_valid: false, is_complete: true Inspect stage findings and correct the rejected invoice data. is_complete: false Required context or a validation stage is missing. Resolve the gap before treating the invoice as checked. Execution error The check could not finish normally. Inspect the error and any attached partial report.

Findings include a stage, code, and message. Warnings alone do not make an otherwise valid report fail. Do not discard them or reduce every failure to a generic “invalid invoice.”

docs.title: Understand the coverage
docs.text:
The local profile implements the pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8 adaptations of CEN and Saudi rules: 105 CEN assertion sites and 152 Saudi sites. It runs without an external SDK runtime and uses the same profile in every API environment.

Under this profile, standard invoices skip signature and QR checks. Simplified invoices check the embedded certificate's key, reference digests, signature, and QR fields. These establish local integrity, not certificate issuer trust.

The default evaluation time is a single current UTC snapshot. For a reproducible historical test, supply an explicit evaluation time as documented in the validation options. A fixed demonstration clock should not become the default for your live integration.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Schema rejection Read the XML/schema error and correct the indicated structure or value. Incomplete predecessor check Supply the trusted previous-invoice hash from your invoice history. Signature/QR findings on the sample The downloaded invoice.xml is unsigned. To examine signed input, replace it with your signed XML and its matching predecessor context. Different results after editing XML Run checks on the exact document you plan to submit; edits can invalidate signature material.

Next, submit the invoice and check gateway acceptance. The validation reference covers report fields and error contracts; SDK compatibility records differences from the SDK.

docs.title: ZATCA API client
docs.text: The API client requests credentials and submits signed invoices to the selected environment. For a runnable integration, start with the API guide. This reference describes inputs, returned data, and how to distinguish a completed request from an accepted invoice.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text:
Operation Required input Returns Behavior Issue compliance credentials CSR and OTP Compliance credentials (CCSID) Sends the CSR as Base64-encoded PEM. Issue production credentials Compliance credentials with a request ID Production credentials (PCSID) Uses the compliance request ID to request production credentials. Renew production credentials Existing production credentials, new CSR, OTP, response language Production credentials Submits a renewal request. Check invoice compliance Signed invoice and compliance credentials Validation response Checks the invoice; a passing check does not establish reporting or clearance. Report a simplified invoice Signed simplified invoice, production credentials, clearance flag, response language Validation response Rejects standard invoices before sending. Clear a standard invoice Signed standard invoice, production credentials, clearance flag, response language Validation response Rejects simplified invoices before sending.

Credentials must match the client's environment. Production credentials describe the credential scope; they can belong to a test environment. The credential constructor stores supplied values; it does not authenticate them or obtain a certificate. Preserve the request ID returned during compliance onboarding.

docs.title: Input values
docs.text: Input Expected value Notes Configuration Selected environment Used for endpoints and credential environment checks. CSR Parsed or generated certificate signing request See CSR reference. Supply the matching private key separately when signing invoices. OTP Text supplied for the onboarding or renewal operation Sent in the OTP header. Invalid HTTP-header characters fail before transport. Token Binary security token returned by ZATCA Used with the secret for HTTP Basic authentication. Secret Credential secret returned by ZATCA Keep credentials out of logs. Request ID Optional text from credential issuance Required to request production credentials from compliance credentials. Invoice Signed invoice object The client sends its hash, UUID, and Base64 XML. Clearance flag Boolean Sends Clearance-Status: 1 when true, 0 when false. It does not change the selected operation. Response language ar, en, or omitted Only the exact value ar selects Arabic; every other value sends English.

docs.title: Interpret an invoice response
docs.text:
A successful HTTP status means that a response body was decoded. Check acceptance before treating an invoice as reported or cleared. The acceptance helper fails for both rejected and unknown outcomes.

Invoked operation Accepted status Rejected status Reporting REPORTED NOT_REPORTED Clearance CLEARED NOT_CLEARED Compliance Validation status PASS or WARNING Validation status ERROR

Missing or unrecognized endpoint status produces an unknown outcome. A positive status accompanied by validation errors also produces an unknown outcome. Warnings alone do not prevent acceptance. Only the status for the operation actually invoked determines its outcome.

Returned field Value Meaning HTTP status Optional integer Actual response status, when attached by the client. Outcome Accepted, rejected, or unknown Classification for the invoked operation. Validation results Result object Contains message collections and optional overall status. Reporting / clearance status Optional text Raw gateway status for each operation. Seller / buyer QR status Optional text Raw QR status returned by the gateway. Cleared invoice Base64 Optional text Exact encoded invoice returned by clearance. Cleared invoice XML Optional decoded text Preserves returned text; does not parse XML or verify its signature.

Missing cleared XML is independent of acceptance. A present empty Base64 value, invalid Base64, NUL bytes, or invalid UTF-8 fails decoding.

Validation results contain information, warning, and error message collections, which can be empty, plus an optional status. Each message has optional type, code, category, message text, and status fields. Handle missing fields instead of assuming that every response contains a complete diagnostic.

docs.title: HTTP failures and custom transport
docs.text:
Invoice operations treat every non-2xx response as an error, including 400 and 409. A duplicate-reporting 409 does not establish that an earlier submission was rejected. A 208 clearance response follows the successful-response path and still requires an acceptance check. Redirects are not followed; a 303 does not trigger automatic reporting. A malformed successful body is a decoding error, and a failed body read is a transport error.

Credential issuance requires a successful response. Renewal additionally supports the gateway's 428 renewal response when it contains a decodable credential body.

Where exposed, prepared requests let you use your own HTTP transport. Preparing performs input checks and builds an owned request without sending it. Send its method, URL, headers, and body, then pass the actual HTTP status and response bytes to its decoder. Headers contain credentials. The decoder preserves the operation context needed for acceptance checks. Keep redirects disabled in custom transports.

Add prepare_ after fatoora_zatca_client_ in the six HTTP function names above. Inputs are identical; the output changes to FatooraComplianceRequest ** for CSR issuance, FatooraProductionRequest ** for production issuance/renewal, or FatooraInvoiceRequest ** for invoice operations.

Request accessors use fatoora_compliance_request_, fatoora_production_request_, or fatoora_invoice_request_. method, url, and headers_json take self, char **out, and error; body uses FatooraBytes **out. decode takes self, uint16_t status, const uint8_t *body, size_t body_len, the matching credential/response output pointer, and error. The request owns its data and does not send HTTP until your transport does so.

Ownership

Outputs and response children are independent owned copies. Release text with fatoora_string_free; release handles with their matching _free function, such as fatoora_zatca_client_free, fatoora_csid_compliance_free, fatoora_csid_production_free, fatoora_validation_response_free, fatoora_validation_results_free, fatoora_validation_message_free, or fatoora_invoice_request_free. See C ownership and errors.

docs.title: CSR and private keys
docs.text: A certificate signing request (CSR) binds a device identity to a public key. Create properties, generate or load a private key, then build the CSR for the selected environment. For a complete runnable workflow, follow Generate a CSR and private key.

docs.title: Property values
docs.text:
Every field is required. The constructor and properties-file parser apply the same validation. Supply your own registered identity values for onboarding; the example properties file contains demonstration data.

Field / properties-file key Expected value common_name / csr.common.name Device or solution common name. serial_number / csr.serial.number Solution serial number in the format required for your device. organization_identifier / csr.organization.identifier Organization VAT identifier. organization_unit_name / csr.organization.unit.name Branch or organizational unit. organization_name / csr.organization.name Legal organization name. country_name / csr.country.name Exactly two ASCII letters, such as SA. invoice_type / csr.invoice.type Exactly four 0 or 1 digits, such as 1100. location_address / csr.location.address Business location. industry_business_category / csr.industry.business.category Business activity.

Text fields must contain non-whitespace text and cannot contain ! @ # $ % & * _ <. Country and invoice-type fields have the stricter formats above. Values are not trimmed or normalized by the constructor. Country validation checks the two-letter format, not membership in the ISO country list. Serial numbers and organization identifiers are not checked against registration records. Passing local validation does not guarantee that ZATCA accepts the identity.

Properties text uses key=value entries. Missing required keys fail; unknown keys are ignored and repeated keys use their last value. File-loading methods read UTF-8.

Parse properties Properties text or a file path Validated properties; fails on unreadable files, malformed text, or missing fields. Generate a key No input A new random secp256k1 private key. Load a key PKCS#8 PEM text or DER bytes Private key; malformed or incompatible key material fails. Build a CSR Properties, private key, environment New CSR signed by the supplied key; properties and key remain usable. Load a CSR DER bytes Parsed CSR; this does not establish gateway approval. Read subject CSR Formatted distinguished-name text. Read extensions CSR Collection of encoded extension values for inspection. Output format Contents Typical use Key PEM / DER PKCS#8 private-key material Save or reload the signing key. CSR PEM Text with certificate-request delimiters Save a readable csr.pem file. CSR DER Binary certificate request Binary storage or parsing. CSR Base64 Base64 of DER bytes Consumers that explicitly require encoded DER. CSR PEM Base64 Base64 of complete PEM text ZATCA credential requests; the API client performs this conversion.

Keep the private key: the CSR contains its public key, not the private key needed for invoice signing. Serialization returns data and does not write files.

docs.title: Errors and diagnostics
docs.text: Use error codes and structured fields to decide how to recover. Messages are intended for display and can change; do not parse their wording.

docs.title: Shared classification
docs.text:
Code Category Meaning 1 InvalidInput An argument, key, certificate, option or context is invalid 2 Validation A model validation failure or interrupted rule evaluation 3 Parse Structured data, a successful API response, or returned cleared XML could not be decoded 4 Xml An XML operation failed 5 Crypto A cryptographic operation failed 6 Io A file or other I/O operation failed 7 Network A network operation failed 8 Unauthorized The service rejected authorization 9 Internal An internal operation failed 10 Api A non-authorization API response or acceptance check failed

Classification follows the cause: an XML failure during signing is Xml, while a file-read failure is Io. Preserve unknown numeric codes and provide a generic fallback. An Internal failure may leave an operation consumed; discard affected operation handles.

docs.title: Handle an error
JSON details
docs.text:
Every details object contains a type string. The schema is explicitly mapped from errors rather than language-specific serialization. Existing field meanings and discriminator strings are stable. Additional fields and types may be added. Consumers must ignore unknown fields and handle unknown types. Messages are for display and must not be parsed for classification.

An invoice validation failure looks like this:

{
  "type": "invoice_validation",
  "issues": [
    {
      "field": "line_item_vat_amount",
      "kind": "mismatch",
      "line_item_index": 0,
      "supplied": "10",
      "expected": "15"
    }
  ]
}

Issue fields use snake_case names for invoice fields. Issue kinds are missing, empty, invalid_format, out_of_range, or mismatch. line_item_index is zero-based, or null for an invoice-level issue. Decimal values are exact strings with insignificant trailing zeroes removed; absent amounts are null.

Details type Structured fields invoice_validation issues: field, kind, item index, supplied and expected amounts schema_parse, schema_validation diagnostics: message, optional file, line, column, severity zatca_validation_execution kind, optional stage, assertion_site, location, diagnostics, and partial report xml_serialize, signing_xml, signing_input diagnostics api_response http_status: actual HTTP status; body: response text; response: complete parsed JSON or null api_response_decode http_status, body, message for a malformed 2xx response api_response_read http_status, message for a failed response-body read api_not_accepted http_status or null, outcome: rejected or unknown, response: typed validation body api_cleared_invoice http_status or null, message for invalid cleared-invoice content api_unauthorized response: timestamp, status, error, message api_server response: category, code, message missing_property path, key properties_parse path, diagnostics io path, diagnostics der_encode context, diagnostics csr_extension extension, diagnostics missing_field field invalid_value field, value invalid_xsd_path path invalid_environment, invalid_country_code, invalid_currency_code, invalid_timestamp, invalid_issue_date value qr_value_too_long tag, length, limit (255 bytes) qr_encoded_too_long length, limit (700 encoded characters)

Message-only failures use diagnostics containing a message. Their types are xml_parse, xpath, qr_xml, signing, invalid_subject, invalid_san, csr_request, csr_build, key_decode, key_encode, csr_validation, network, invalid_response, http, and client_state.

Types without additional fields are invalid_decimal, decimal_out_of_range, missing_seller_vat, missing_seller_name, missing_buyer_id, and invalid_vat_format. Binding-level failures use {"type":"binding_error"} with the classification and message available through their accessors.

Diagnostic location fields may be absent or null. File paths are converted to UTF-8 lossily when their native encoding cannot be represented. Nested signing and invoice-import failures retain their underlying validation, serialization, decimal, or QR details.

docs.title: Local ZATCA execution failures
docs.text:
Local validation returns a report for ordinary rejection or incomplete coverage. Inspect is_valid before accepting an invoice. is_complete describes stage coverage; has_errors includes findings obtained before a stage failed. Warnings allow validity once all required stages complete.

Interrupted execution produces an error. Its details have type zatca_validation_execution and these fields:

Field Meaning kind Execution failure kind from the table below stage xsd, cen, ksa, signature, qr, previous_invoice_hash, or null assertion_site Source assertion key, such as ksa:112:BR-KSA-CL-02, or null location Shared validation location, including namespace-independent XPath, or null diagnostics One diagnostic containing the execution failure's message report Full report up to the failure, with stage statuses and earlier findings Execution kind Shared classification invalid_xml Xml (4) unsupported_xml InvalidInput (1) capacity_exceeded InvalidInput (1) invalid_context InvalidInput (1) rule_evaluation Validation (2) schema Parse (3) integrity Crypto (5)

The rule_evaluation classification describes interrupted execution. Ordinary business-rule violations remain findings in a successfully returned report. Invalid arguments or malformed options can fail before validation starts and have no partial report. Always allow for that absence. See invoice validation for stage applicability and predecessor context.

docs.title: Invoice model
docs.text: Use the invoice model to assemble invoice data, calculate totals, and inspect imported or signed invoices. For an existing XML document, start with XML parsing. For signatures and certificate inputs, see invoice signing.

docs.title: Building an invoice
docs.text:
Create a builder, set the required fields, append one or more line items, then build a finalized invoice. Building checks supported field formats and amounts and calculates totals. It does not run schema validation, all ZATCA business rules, or signature verification; use validation for those checks.

Repeated configuration replaces the previous value. Adding a line item appends it in insertion order. An allowance sets the invoice-level discount and its reason; it does not add a second discount.

docs.title: Fields and expected values
docs.text:
Field Required Expected value and behavior Invoice type and subtype Yes Tax invoice, prepayment, credit note, or debit note; standard or simplified subtype. Credit/debit notes also need an original invoice ID and reason. Original UUID and issue date are optional. ID Yes Nonblank invoice identifier, such as INV-1001. UUID Yes Invoice UUID text. The builder checks nonblank input, not UUID syntax. Issue datetime Yes UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, for example 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z. Currency Yes Recognized ISO currency code, such as SAR. Trimmed and normalized to uppercase. Previous invoice hash Yes Previous invoice hash text. The builder checks nonblank input; it does not verify the chain or decode the hash. Invoice counter Yes Unsigned 64-bit integer. The model accepts zero; check applicable business rules separately. Seller Yes Name, address, and VAT ID; optional other identification and scheme. Buyer No in builder Name and address, plus VAT ID or other identification. A supplied buyer must have at least one identifier. Additional requirements depend on invoice business rules. Payment means code Yes Nonblank code text, for example 10 for cash. The builder does not validate the complete payment code list. VAT category Yes Standard, zero-rated, exempt, or out of scope. Each line also has its own category. Line items Yes At least one. Nonblank description and unit code; nonnegative quantity and unit price. VAT rate Per line Percentage from 0 to 100, at most two decimal places. Categories other than standard require zero. Invoice charge / discount No Nonnegative decimal amount, at most two decimal places. Defaults to zero. Note No Language code and text. Flags No Third party, nominal, export, summary, self-billed. Defaults to no flags.

Address inputs are country code, city, street, building number, and postal code, with optional additional street, additional number, and district. Country accepts recognized ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 values (SA or SAU) and is stored as alpha-3. A VAT ID wrapper checks only that trimmed text is nonempty; use ZATCA validation for country-specific requirements.

Credit/debit note original issue dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Optional values mean absence; an empty string is still a supplied value.

See decimal numbers for precision and rounding. Line totals are calculated from quantity and price. Explicitly supplied line totals must match the rounded calculation; imported amounts are not accepted merely because they parse.

docs.title: Returned data and totals
docs.text:
A finalized invoice contains invoice data and calculated totals. A signed invoice additionally contains signed XML, QR payload, and signature metadata. Importing a signed invoice does not prove its signature is valid.

Result Contents Invoice data Identity, type/subtype, parties, notes, original invoice reference, flags, line items, and invoice adjustments. Line item Description, quantity, unit code, unit price, line total, VAT rate, VAT amount, and category. Indexed access is zero-based and rejects out-of-range indexes. Totals Line extension, allowance total, charge total, taxable amount, tax amount, tax inclusive total, prepaid amount, payable rounding amount, and payable amount. Model hash Base64 hash calculated by serializing the finalized invoice model. On imported signed documents this can differ from the embedded invoice hash.

docs.title: Invoice signing reference
docs.text: Create a signer from an X.509 certificate and an unencrypted secp256k1 private key in PKCS#8 format. Use it to sign a finalized invoice or existing XML. For a complete workflow, see the signing guide.

docs.title: Inputs and behavior
docs.text:
Operation Expected input Result and behavior Create from PEM Certificate PEM and private-key PEM text A reusable signer; rejects invalid certificate/key encodings Create from DER Certificate DER bytes and private-key PKCS#8 DER bytes A reusable signer with the same behavior as PEM construction Export certificate Live signer Certificate as PEM text or DER bytes Sign finalized invoice A finalized invoice and a live signer A signed invoice; consumes the finalized invoice's state Sign existing XML UBL invoice XML text Signed XML text; preserves bytes outside the signing structures it owns. Re-signing requires the same certificate Hash existing XML XML text Base64 invoice digest after invoice-specific exclusions and canonicalization

Signer construction parses the certificate and key; it does not establish that they match, that the certificate is trusted, or that its dates are valid. Signing checks that the private key matches the certificate and rejects a mismatch. It does not run the complete invoice validator. Validate the resulting XML separately when you need a local compliance report.

Keep signed XML unchanged for storage and submission. Signing existing XML does not construct an invoice model or run all model-import checks.

docs.title: Signed invoice values
docs.text:
All getters below leave the signed invoice usable. Values extracted from imported signed XML are metadata, not proof of signature verification.

Value Returned content XML Original stored signed XML text XML Base64 Base64 of that stored XML text QR code Base64 TLV payload for rendering; see QR reference Invoice hash Embedded invoice digest from signature metadata Model hash Recomputed hash of the underlying finalized model's serialization; not an alias for the embedded hash Signature Encoded invoice signature Public key Encoded public-key material ZATCA key signature Optional encoded certificate-signature material Issuer / serial Certificate issuer and serial from signed properties Certificate hash Encoded certificate digest Signed properties hash Encoded signed-properties digest Signing time UTC text in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS format
