docs.title: Methods by language
Invoice validation
docs.text: Validate the original invoice XML before relying on its structure or business-rule results. Choose a schema check for UBL structure, or a local ZATCA report for schema, business rules, and applicable integrity checks. For a runnable example, see the validation guide.

docs.title: Choose the check
docs.text:
Operation What it establishes Build an invoice Implemented field, range, and amount checks; calculated totals. Parse invoice XML Supported fields and supplied amounts can be represented by the invoice model. Validate the schema Conformance to the bundled UBL 2.1 schema. Run local ZATCA validation Results and coverage for the local profile's schema, business rules, signature, QR, and predecessor checks. Sign an invoice Signature material was generated; no implicit business-rule validation. Parse a signed invoice Signature material was extracted; no implicit authenticity check.

No local result proves remote acceptance, certificate issuer trust, or revocation status. Integrity checks verify supported algorithms and references, bind the embedded key to the signature, and compare QR data with the invoice and certificate.

docs.title: Inputs and options
docs.text:
All checks take complete invoice XML text and a configuration object. Pass original XML, not Base64 or a file path. Schema checks use bundled resources and do not need network access. Malformed XML is rejected rather than repaired.

Local validation additionally accepts these optional context values:

Option Expected value If omitted previous_invoice_hash Canonical Base64 SHA-256 digest, or the SDK's Base64-encoded hexadecimal digest representation. This is the expected predecessor hash, compared with the invoice's PIH. Predecessor stage reports context_required; the report is incomplete and is_valid is false. evaluated_at RFC3339 instant with timezone, such as 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z or 2026-10-15T12:30:00+03:00. One clock snapshot is used for the validation run.

The validator cannot obtain invoice history. Supply predecessor context from your own invoice sequence. An empty string is not an omitted option. APIs that accept options as JSON require an object containing only these keys, with string or null values. The encoded options input is limited to 4 KiB (4096 bytes); unknown keys and malformed values are rejected.

docs.title: Local ZATCA report
docs.text:
A completed function call means a report was produced. Always inspect is_valid; rejected invoices and incomplete coverage can both be returned without an execution error.

Report field Value and meaning schema_version Report format version, currently 1. profile Local validation profile identifier, currently zatca-sdk-238-R3.4.8. evaluated_at The evaluation clock snapshot, including offset. stages Ordered stage results: xsd, cen, ksa, signature, qr, previous_invoice_hash. is_complete All required stages completed exactly once; explicitly inapplicable signature/QR stages count as covered. has_errors At least one error finding exists, including findings from partial stages. is_valid Complete coverage with no error findings. Warnings do not make this false.

Each stage contains stage, status, findings, evaluated_assertions (the assertion sites evaluated), and optional provenance with source stylesheet and sha256. Provenance identifies the rules used; applications can retain it alongside reports for traceability.

Stage Checks xsd Bundled UBL XML structure. cen Applicable European invoice business rules in the selected profile. ksa Applicable Saudi invoice business rules in the selected profile. signature Local signature integrity; skipped as inapplicable for standard invoices under this profile. qr QR integrity and consistency; skipped as inapplicable for standard invoices under this profile. previous_invoice_hash Invoice PIH compared with supplied predecessor context. Stage status Meaning completed Checks finished; findings may still contain errors. not_run A dependency failed or execution stopped earlier. not_applicable The selected profile does not require this stage for this invoice. context_required Required predecessor context was not supplied. evaluation_failed Execution stopped before completion; findings may be partial.

Schema rejection returns a report and skips dependent stages. A report with no findings is not sufficient by itself: it can be incomplete. For example, missing predecessor context can yield has_errors: false, is_complete: false, and is_valid: false.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Finding field Meaning layer field_checks, xsd, business_rules, signature, qr, or previous_invoice_hash. code Stable rule or library identifier; use this for programmatic handling. severity warning or error. message Human-readable explanation. Wording is not a stable API. location Optional model field path, XPath, or XML source coordinates. assertion_site Optional source assertion identifier on local ZATCA findings.

Field paths use zero-based indexes, such as line_items[0].quantity. XML line and column positions are one-based. Business-rule findings use XPath locations against the original document; some findings have no reliable location.

Field codes include FIELD_REQUIRED, FIELD_EMPTY, FIELD_INVALID_FORMAT, FIELD_OUT_OF_RANGE, and FIELD_MISMATCH. Schema violations use XSD_INVALID. Business-rule findings use their implemented rule codes.

docs.title: Execution failures and partial results
docs.text:
An invalid invoice is different from a check that could not finish. Malformed XML, unsupported DTDs, capacity limits, invalid context, and rule/integrity execution failures produce an error. When validation has started, the error carries the partial report and all findings collected so far.

Execution details include kind, optional stage, assertion_site, location, and report. The error message is exposed directly or in diagnostics, depending on the language API. Failure kinds are invalid_xml, unsupported_xml, capacity_exceeded, invalid_context, rule_evaluation, schema, and integrity. Invalid options rejected before validation starts need not carry a report. Never treat partial findings as complete coverage. See errors for the shared error contract.

docs.title: Language reference
Decimal numbers and rounding
docs.text: Use decimal strings or integers for invoice amounts. Parsing never silently rounds an input.

docs.title: Representation
docs.text:
Accepted syntax is [+-]digits[.digits], using ASCII digits. Whitespace, exponents, separators, infinities and NaN are rejected. Parsing never rounds. The range is a signed 96-bit coefficient with a scale from 0 through 28. Values outside that range fail with an out-of-range error.

Equality compares numeric values: 1.0 equals 1.00. Display and JSON use canonical decimal strings, without exponents or unnecessary trailing zeros. Negative zero is displayed as 0. XML monetary fields use two decimal places; quantities and unit prices retain their supported precision.

Arithmetic uses checked signed 128-bit integer intermediates. If an intermediate coefficient or the final decimal cannot be represented, calculation returns an error. Precision is never reduced to make an intermediate fit.

docs.title: Calculation boundaries
docs.text:
The calculation contract follows section 10 and the field-specific decimal constraints in the ZATCA XML standard, May 2023.

  • Line net: calculate quantity × unit price, then round half-up to two decimals.
  • Calculated line VAT: calculate quantity × unit price × rate / 100, then round once to two decimals. Do not round the intermediate product first.
  • Group lines by VAT category and rate. Sum their finalized line net amounts and apply the document discounts and charges assigned to that group.
  • Category VAT: multiply that taxable base by its rate, divide by 100, then round half-up to two decimals. Document VAT is the sum of these category VAT amounts.
  • Document totals use the finalized amounts. XML and QR rendering consume those totals without introducing another calculation stage.

For three lines of 0.03 at 15%, each calculated line VAT is 0.00, while document VAT is 0.01.

Rates must be between 0 and 100 with at most two decimal places. Supplied amounts such as document discounts and charges must already have at most two decimals. Nonstandard VAT categories require a zero rate. Negative invoice line values and negative discounts/charges are rejected by the builder. Credit notes use positive amounts with the appropriate document type. A supplied signed payable-rounding adjustment is preserved exactly; it is not rounded during import.

The builder's document VAT category assigns its scalar discount and charge to one matching category/rate group. If several rates match, building fails. XML imports can resolve that rate from the adjustment's explicit tax category. Multiple adjustment category/rate groups require a richer adjustment model and are rejected.

docs.title: Calculated and supplied values
docs.text:
Line-item construction calculates amounts. Importing supplied totals validates them against those calculations exactly; mismatches return validation issues containing the supplied and expected values.

XML import preserves supplied line VAT. The May 2023 standard removed BR-KSA-50; BR-KSA-51 still relates line gross to line net plus supplied VAT. Import validates amount precision, the line net calculation, line gross when present, document adjustments, supplied category subtotals and document totals. It preserves prepaid amounts and payable-rounding adjustments and checks the payable equation.

This numeric validation covers the model's supported calculations. It does not replace the complete ZATCA business-rule validator or add line allowances, line charges or price-base quantities to the model.

docs.title: XML and schemas
docs.text: The library reads and writes UBL invoice XML and includes the UBL 2.1 invoice schema. Validation uses bundled resources and does not download schemas from locations supplied by an invoice. No SDK installation or network access is needed.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text: Operation Input Result and guarantee Parse XML Invoice XML text A supported invoice model with field and amount checks; not a complete compliance check Validate the schema Original XML and configuration Checks element structure, attributes and schema types Validate locally Original XML, configuration and predecessor context A report covering schema, business rules and applicable integrity checks Hash XML Original XML text Base64 invoice digest after invoice-specific exclusions and canonicalization Sign XML XML, certificate and private key Signed XML; signing alone does not establish compliance

docs.title: Decimal values
docs.text:
The bundled schema's amount, measure, numeric and quantity fields accept XML decimal syntax without imposing a machine floating-point range. This preserves schema validation for large decimal values. An extension that directly uses xs:decimal can still encounter the schema engine's numeric capacity limit.

Invoice-model calculations and business-rule validation have separate precision and capacity limits. Passing schema validation does not mean a value can be calculated by the model. See decimal numbers and rounding.

docs.title: Hashing and signed XML
docs.text:
Invoice hashing applies the invoice-specific exclusions and C14N 1.1 canonicalization before calculating the digest. It is not a hash of the raw file bytes. Keep the returned signed XML unchanged when storing or submitting it: formatting or rebuilding it can change signature-relevant content.

Parsing a signed invoice reads its embedded signature metadata; it does not verify the signature, certificate issuer trust or remote acceptance. Use the validation report to determine which checks actually completed.

docs.title: Invoice XML
docs.text: Use these APIs to read invoice XML into an invoice model, serialize a finalized invoice, or retrieve the exact XML stored by a signed invoice. For a walkthrough, see invoice signing or validation.

Supplied supported amounts are checked against calculations. Parse signed invoice Complete signed invoice XML text or a file path A signed invoice containing signature metadata and the exact supplied XML text. Parsing does not verify the signature. Serialize finalized invoice Finalized invoice XML text with default two-space indentation. Serialization creates a document from the model; it is not a lossless XML editor. Read signed XML Signed invoice Exact stored XML, without formatting changes. Newly signed invoices store the output of signing; imported invoices store the input text. Take signed XML Signed invoice Exact stored XML and consumption of the invoice state. Encode signed XML Signed invoice Base64 of the stored XML, suitable for APIs that require encoded invoice content.

Text inputs contain XML, not Base64 or a filename. File variants take a local filesystem path and read its contents as text. Parsing can fail on malformed XML, unsupported or missing required fields, or inconsistent supplied amounts. File operations can also fail when the path cannot be read.

Parsing and serialization do not establish schema conformance, business-rule compliance, or invoice acceptance. Run validation explicitly when needed.

docs.title: Preserve signed XML
docs.text: Keep returned signed XML unchanged when saving or submitting it. Do not pretty-print, normalize whitespace, or reconstruct it from invoice data. Reading metadata does not change the stored XML. For edits followed by signing, see invoice signing.

docs.title: C and C++ bindings
docs.text:
Use the native library to create CSRs, build and sign invoices, validate XML and call the ZATCA API. Headers and the shared library must come from the same release. Download them from the release assets.

Configure your runtime loader to find the shared library: .so on Linux, .dylib on macOS, or the DLL on Windows. Select your language for its include paths, return values and cleanup rules.

CC++

Include one header, check the shared status, and release returned owners. Passing NULL as the error argument is supported when only the status matters. The deliberately incomplete invoice below fails validation.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    FatooraConfig *config = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    bool valid = false;
    FatooraStatus status = fatoora_config_new(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &config, &error);
    if (status == FATOORA_OK)
        status = fatoora_xml_validate(config, "<Invoice></Invoice>", &valid, &error);
    if (status == FATOORA_OK) printf("valid: %s\n", valid ? "true" : "false");
    else fprintf(stderr, "error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    fatoora_config_free(config);
    return status == FATOORA_OK && valid ? 0 : 1;
}

String getters return owned char * values through output pointers; release them with fatoora_string_free(). Optional text returns NULL for absence and an allocated empty string for a present empty value. Decimal values are exact strings. Constructors and line items use named-field option structs. See the complete builder example and the ownership rules below.

Compile and link

Use matching headers and native libraries from the same release. Compile bindings/c/fatoora.c once alongside your application, include bindings/c, and link fatoora_ffi:

cc -std=c11 validate.c bindings/c/fatoora.c \
  -Ibindings/c -L/path/to/native-library -lfatoora_ffi -o validate

Release archives use include/fatoora.h, src/fatoora.c and include/generated/. Compile the archive's src/fatoora.c with -Iinclude and link the matching native library. If your application is C++, compile this adapter as C, then link the object into your application.

Values and ownership

Value Contract Text input Borrowed NUL-terminated UTF-8 for the duration of the call Optional text input NULL means absent; "" is present empty text Decimal input Exact decimal string; no exponent or whitespace Text output Owned char *; free with fatoora_string_free Object output Owned opaque handle; free with its fatoora_<type>_free function Byte output FatooraBytes owner; its data view borrows from that owner Error Owned FatooraError; its message and details strings borrow from the error Output arguments Cleared on entry; free any old value before reusing its slot

Invoice, party, address and response getters return independent owned snapshots. They survive destruction of the source object. Optional owned output is NULL when absent. Freeing a null owner is safe. Passing NULL for the error-output slot discards detailed diagnostics but retains the returned status.

Do not copy opaque owners by value or free them with the system allocator. FATOORA_OK from local invoice validation means a report was produced; inspect is_valid in that report.

C++ headers provide their own C-linkage declarations. Include them directly; no external extern "C" wrapper is needed. They return diplomat::result and manage objects with std::unique_ptr. Inspect is_ok(), then move the result's .ok() or .err() value to take ownership. Owners release their native objects automatically.

#include "fatoora/BindingError.hpp"
#include "fatoora/Config.hpp"
#include "fatoora/Xml.hpp"
#include <iostream>
#include <utility>

int main() {
    auto created = fatoora::Config::new_(0);
    if (!created.is_ok()) {
        auto error = std::move(created).err().value();
        std::cerr << error->code() << ": " << error->message() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    auto config = std::move(created).ok().value();
    auto result = fatoora::Xml::validate(*config, "<Invoice></Invoice>");
    if (!result.is_ok()) {
        auto error = std::move(result).err().value();
        std::cerr << error->code() << ": " << error->message() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    return std::move(result).ok().value() ? 0 : 1;
}

Fallible C++ text accessors return a result containing std::string; error text accessors return std::string directly. Owned strings survive destruction of their source objects. Byte spans still borrow from their Bytes owner.

Compile and link

Use C++17 or later and headers matching the native library release:

c++ -std=c++17 validate.cpp -Ibindings/cpp \
  -L/path/to/native-library -lfatoora_ffi -o validate_cpp

Text inputs are borrowed for the call. Decimal inputs and outputs use exact strings. Optional text can be an absent owner; inspect the result before dereferencing it. Returned invoice, party, address and response objects are independent snapshots. Keep a Bytes owner alive while using its byte span.

docs.title: Consumption and safety
docs.text:
Builder input errors allow correction. build() consumes the builder's inner state even when final validation fails. Signing consumes a finalized invoice, and the consuming XML getter consumes a signed invoice. Subsequent operations on a consumed owner return an error; the owner remains safe to destroy.

Callers must provide valid pointers, preserve borrowed storage lifetimes, and synchronize mutable access, consumption, and destruction. Malformed bytes are validated only after the caller has supplied a valid byte view. Invalid pointers, double destruction, and concurrent conflicting access violate the native contract.

Fallible operations catch unwinding Rust panics and return Internal errors. Abort-mode panics and allocation aborts cannot be recovered this way. A panic can leave an operation consumed; discard the affected owner after an Internal failure. See errors for numeric codes and structured details.

docs.text: Use the Fatoority NuGet package to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests from .NET 8 or later. Public classes use the Fatoora namespace. The package includes the native library for its supported platforms.

docs.text:
In your application project, install the published package:

dotnet add package Fatoority

Use the Fatoora namespace. Check the supported native platforms below before deploying your application.

Runtime identifier Platform linux-x64 Linux x86-64, glibc 2.28 or later win-x64 Windows x86-64 osx-arm64 macOS Apple Silicon

Match your application's OS and architecture to a packaged runtime identifier. NuGet supplies the native asset at runtime; no library search-path override is needed. Linux musl/Alpine is not included. A package built locally inherits its build host's libc requirements.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Import Fatoora and dispose native objects when finished:

using Fatoora;

using var config = Config.New(0);
using var key = SigningKey.Generate();
using var bytes = key.ToDer();
using var view = bytes.AsSlice();
byte[] privateKey = view.Clone();

privateKey is an independent managed copy. Keep it secure; disposing the native objects does not erase that array. Follow the CSR guide for a complete credential-generation workflow.

Use environment 0 for nonproduction, 1 for simulation, and 2 for production. Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree on the environment. See the CSR, signing, validation, and QR guides for complete C# examples.

docs.title: Values and ownership
Errors
docs.text:
public static void ShowError()
    {
        try
        {
            using var key = SigningKey.FromPem("invalid key");
        }
        catch (BindingErrorException error)
        {
            using var details = error.Inner;
            Console.WriteLine($"{details.Code()}: {error.Message}");
            Console.WriteLine(details.DetailsJson());
        }
    }

BindingErrorException.Message contains the native message. Inner.Code() uses the shared error codes, and Inner.DetailsJson() preserves structured details such as HTTP status and response body. Dispose Inner after reading it. Invalid UTF-16 fails before the native call with EncoderFallbackException; invalid native inputs, including embedded NUL, use BindingErrorException.

docs.title: API requests
docs.text:
Create a client with ZatcaClient.Create(config). Dispose the client, credentials, and responses with using. The following methods return owned objects:

Method Inputs Returns PostCsrForCcsid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP string CsidCompliance PostCcsidForPcsid(credentials) CsidCompliance CsidProduction RenewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage) CsidProduction, Csr, OTP, nullable language string CsidProduction CheckInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials) SignedInvoice, CsidCompliance ValidationResponse ReportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, nullable language string ValidationResponse ClearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, nullable language string ValidationResponse

All listed arguments are required, including nullable arguments: pass null when no language override is needed. clearanceStatus sets the clearance-status request header; use false for ordinary reporting and true for clearance. It does not describe the result of the operation.

The native client methods block the calling thread. HTTP success alone does not establish invoice acceptance: inspect Outcome() or call EnsureAccepted(). For clearance, ClearedInvoiceXml() returns Text?: when present, read Value(), save the text, and dispose the returned owner. See the API guide for rejection, unknown outcomes, and cleared-document semantics.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text:
Blocking method Prepared equivalent Credential scope / result PostCsrForCcsid PreparePostCsrForCcsid CSR and OTP to compliance credentials PostCcsidForPcsid PreparePostCcsidForPcsid Compliance to production credentials RenewCsid PrepareRenewCsid Production credentials, CSR and OTP to renewed credentials CheckInvoiceCompliance PrepareCheckInvoiceCompliance Compliance credentials; validation response ReportSimplifiedInvoice PrepareReportSimplifiedInvoice Production credentials; reporting response ClearStandardInvoice PrepareClearStandardInvoice Production credentials; clearance response

PreparePostCsrForCcsid returns ComplianceRequest; credential exchange and renewal return ProductionRequest; invoice operations return InvoiceRequest. Their arguments match the corresponding blocking method.

For asynchronous HTTP or cancellation, use a Prepare* method and your own HttpClient. The request exposes Method(), Url(), HeadersJson() (a JSON array of header pairs), and an owned Body(). Copy its bytes before awaiting the transport. Pass the HTTP status and response bytes to Decode(ushort, byte[]), including non-2xx responses, so the library can classify gateway errors. Decode returns an owned CsidCompliance, CsidProduction, or ValidationResponse matching the request type; dispose it after use. Configure the transport to refuse redirects, and pass your cancellation token to send/read operations. The generated blocking methods do not accept a cancellation token.

Prepared requests own their wire data, credentials, and decoding context; keep the request alive until decoding completes. Headers contain credentials and should not be logged.

docs.text: Use fatoority in Node.js or a browser to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests. The package includes WebAssembly and TypeScript declarations. For a complete task walkthrough, start with the guides.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
npm install fatoority

Import from the package root for asynchronous API requests and validation with an automatically supplied clock:

import { Config, SigningKey, Xml, ZatcaClient } from 'fatoority';

const config = Config.new_(0);
const key = SigningKey.generate();
const privateKeyPem = key.toPem();

The private key is secret material; store it securely. Environment values are 0 (nonproduction), 1 (simulation), and 2 (production). Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree.

Node.js 22+ and modern browsers are supported. Browser execution requires WebAssembly, Web Crypto, FinalizationRegistry, and top-level await. TypeScript users can use NodeNext or bundler module resolution; no separate @types package is needed.

Local validation
API requests
docs.text:
Create new ZatcaClient(config) to use the global fetch, or new ZatcaClient(config, { fetch: customFetch }) to provide a compatible transport. All methods below return promises. Optional options accepts { signal }, where signal is an AbortSignal.

Method Inputs Promise result postCsrForCcsid(csr, otp, options?) Csr, OTP string CsidCompliance postCcsidForPcsid(credentials, options?) CsidCompliance CsidProduction renewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage?, options?) See API requests and responses for credential requirements and response fields, and the API guide for a complete workflow.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text:
For your own HTTP integration, import ZatcaClient from fatoority/raw, construct it with ZatcaClient.create(config), and call its prepare* methods. These return ComplianceRequest, ProductionRequest, or InvoiceRequest objects.

Request method Return value method() HTTP method string url() Complete request URL string headersJson() JSON array of header-name/value pairs body() Bytes; use asSlice() for a copied request body decode(status, bytes) Credentials or ValidationResponse, depending on request type; may throw

Prepared requests retain their data and decoding context independently of the original invoice and credentials. Copy the outgoing body before awaiting HTTP. Pass every HTTP status and its response bytes to decode, including non-2xx responses. Disable redirects. Headers contain credentials and should not be logged.

Alternatively, sendPrepared(request, { fetch, signal }) from fatoority performs these steps and returns a promise for the decoded result. It copies the body before awaiting, refuses redirects, and forwards HTTP error responses to decoding.

docs.title: Browser deployment
docs.text:
The loader resolves fatoora_ffi.wasm relative to its package modules. Deploy the modules and WASM together, or configure your bundler to copy WASM to that URL. Serve the application over HTTP(S), with WebAssembly execution and Web Crypto available.

Direct ZATCA requests depend on gateway CORS. Use a server-side transport when needed and decide where credentials and private keys should reside. Local validation runs without Java, external SDK files, or network access.

Use a published release from Maven Central. Java/Kotlin imports remain com.fatoora; the Maven group is com.fatoority.

For desktop Gradle projects, add this to build.gradle.kts:

repositories { mavenCentral() }
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.4.4")
}

dependencies {

docs.title: Ownership and values
docs.text:
Value Public JVM value Native object AutoCloseable; close after use Optional text input Nullable String; null differs from "" Optional text output Nullable Text; read value() and close it Decimal Invariant decimal string Unsigned byte / short / int Checked JVM integer / integer / long Unsigned 64-bit counter BigInteger, range 0 through 2^64−1 Binary input / copied output JVM byte array; copies survive closing their owner Native failure BindingException(code, message, detailsJson)

Close objects returned by methods as well as those you construct. Native errors are copied to managed data and freed immediately; exceptions need no cleanup. Bytes.asSlice() copies bytes under the owner lock, so the returned array survives closing its native owner. Strings reject lone UTF-16 surrogates and embedded NUL.

Calls acquire all participating owners in a fixed lock order. Concurrent calls on the same object serialize; close() waits for active calls and is idempotent. Later calls throw IllegalStateException. Operations on independent owners can run concurrently. Consumed builders/invoices remain closeable but reject further use with a native error. Automatic cleanup is nondeterministic; explicitly close owners. Freeing native memory does not guarantee secret erasure.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Native failures throw BindingException. Its code, message, and JSON details are managed values; exceptions need no cleanup. Invalid UTF-16 and embedded NUL are rejected. Use structured error details to distinguish validation, input, cryptography, and gateway failures.

KotlinJava 
try {
    Config.create(99).use { }
} catch (error: BindingException) {
    println("${error.code}: ${error.message}")
    println(error.detailsJson)
}

try (Config config = Config.create(99)) {
    // An invalid environment throws before this block.
} catch (BindingException error) {
    System.err.println(error.getCode() + ": " + error.getMessage());
    System.err.println(error.getDetailsJson());
}

docs.title: API requests
docs.text:
Create a client with ZatcaClient.create(config). Native HTTP methods block the calling thread and return objects that must be closed:

Method Inputs Returns postCsrForCcsid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP string CsidCompliance postCcsidForPcsid(credentials) CsidCompliance CsidProduction renewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage) CsidProduction, Csr, OTP, nullable language CsidProduction checkInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials) SignedInvoice, CsidCompliance ValidationResponse reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, nullable language ValidationResponse clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, nullable language ValidationResponse

The final acceptLanguage argument can be omitted; its default is null.

clearanceStatus controls the request header; use false for ordinary reporting and true for clearance. acceptLanguage controls the language header; pass null for no override. It does not describe the response outcome.

A returned response is not necessarily accepted. Call outcome() or ensureAccepted(). clearedInvoiceXml() returns nullable Text; read value(), save the cleared XML, and close that owner. See the API reference.

KotlinJava

Coroutine extensions postCsrForCcsidAsync, postCcsidForPcsidAsync, renewCsidAsync, checkInvoiceComplianceAsync, reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync, and clearStandardInvoiceAsync dispatch blocking calls to Dispatchers.IO.

// Inside a suspend function, with live client, invoice, and credentials.
client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, false).use { response ->
    response.ensureAccepted()
}

Keep input owners open until completion. Cancellation cannot interrupt an in-flight native call. If cancellation discards a completed result, the coroutine wrapper closes it. Use a prepared request with a cancellable HTTP transport when you need to interrupt network work.

Blocking methods can run on your application's executor. Cancelling a task does not interrupt an in-flight native HTTP call. Keep its input owners open until completion. Use prepared requests with a cancellable HTTP transport when you need to interrupt network work.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text: prepareReportSimplifiedInvoice, for example, returns an owned InvoiceRequest: read url(), method(), headersJson() and body(), send exactly those values, then call decode(status, responseBytes) and ensureAccepted() on the returned response. HTTP status is a checked integer; the response body is a byte array. Pass non-2xx responses through decoding too, and disable redirects. Close the prepared request, its body owner, and decoded response after use. Prepared requests own their bytes and decoding context independently of the original credentials/invoice. Headers contain credentials: do not log them.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
Use the Android artifact alone. It supplies JNA's Android dependency and shrinker rules and declares the Internet permission. It supports 64-bit ABIs with 16 KiB ELF alignment. Run network, signing, and validation work off the UI thread.

Android native TLS uses bundled Mozilla/WebPKI roots. Android user-installed CAs and app network-security configuration do not modify that trust store. Prepared requests let apps use their own HTTP client and certificate policy.

docs.title: Python package reference
docs.text: Use Python 3.9 or later. Install fatoority and import fatoora to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests. Start with the guides for complete workflows; this page describes Python-specific values and behavior.

docs.title: Install and import
docs.text:
python -m pip install fatoority

from fatoora import Config, Environment, SigningKey

with Config(Environment.NON_PRODUCTION) as config:
    with SigningKey.generate() as key:
        private_key_pem = key.to_pem()

Keep the private key secure. Exported strings and bytes remain in Python memory after the native owner closes.

The default Config() environment is Environment.NON_PRODUCTION. Choose Environment.SIMULATION or Environment.PRODUCTION explicitly when needed. Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree on the environment.

Use exact decimal text such as "0.3333", rather than constructing a Decimal from a binary float. See decimal numbers and rounding.

Public choices use IntEnum members. Prefer their names to raw integers:

Invoice builder timestamps use UTC text such as "2026-01-01T12:00:00Z". Country/currency values are strings; their constructors validate and normalize supported values. See the invoice model.

docs.title: Object lifetime
docs.text:
Native owners support with and close(). Close objects returned by methods as well as ones you construct. Closing is idempotent; later calls on a closed owner raise InvalidInputError. Calls involving the same owners are synchronized. Independent owners can be used independently.

InvoiceBuilder.build() consumes the builder's inner state even when final validation fails. FinalizedInvoice.sign(signer) consumes the finalized invoice; SignedInvoice.into_xml() consumes the signed invoice. The wrapper remains safe to close, but further use of consumed state fails. Create a new input object to retry after a consuming operation fails.

Plain strings, bytes, decimal values, and dataclass snapshots do not need close(). Returned object snapshots are independent of their parent, but still need their own cleanup.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Native failures raise subclasses of FfiError, which inherits FatooraError. Use str(error) for the message, .code for its numeric classification, .kind for FfiErrorKind, and .details for structured data.

from fatoora import SigningKey
from fatoora.errors import FfiError

try:
    SigningKey.from_pem("invalid key")
except FfiError as error:
    print(error.code, str(error))
    print(error.details)
Category Exception Invalid input InvalidInputError Validation rejection ValidationError Parsing ParseError XML XmlError Cryptography CryptoError File access IoError Network NetworkError Authorization UnauthorizedError Internal failure InternalError API response ApiError

Unknown native codes produce FfiError with .kind set to None; .code and .details remain available. Python argument checks can raise TypeError or ValueError before a native call. Do not parse message text to identify an error; use error codes and structured details.

Function Inputs Returns validate_xml_invoice_from_str(config, xml) Config, XML str True on schema success; raises on malformed XML or schema rejection validate_zatca_invoice_from_str(config, xml, *, previous_invoice_hash=None, evaluated_at=None) Config, XML str, optional keyword-only context strings Report dict, including rejection or incomplete coverage invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str(xml) XML str Base64 invoice hash str 
from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import Config, validate_zatca_invoice_from_str

xml = Path("invoice.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
with Config() as config:
    report = validate_zatca_invoice_from_str(config, xml)
print(report["is_valid"], report["is_complete"])

previous_invoice_hash supplies trusted invoice-history context. evaluated_at accepts an RFC3339 timestamp; omission uses one UTC clock snapshot. Missing predecessor context makes coverage incomplete. A returned dictionary does not mean the invoice passed: inspect is_valid and the stage findings.

Execution failures raise an exception and may include a partial report at error.details["report"]. Argument failures can have no report. All schemas are bundled; validation needs no network or external SDK. It does not establish remote acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See the validation reference.

docs.title: ZATCA API methods
docs.text:
Create ZatcaClient(config) with a live Config. Client methods block the calling thread and return owned objects:

Method Inputs Returns post_csr_for_ccsid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP str CsidCompliance post_ccsid_for_pcsid(ccsid) CsidCompliance CsidProduction renew_csid(pcsid, csr, otp, accept_language=None) CsidProduction, Csr, OTP, optional language CsidProduction check_invoice_compliance(invoice, ccsid) SignedInvoice, CsidCompliance ValidationResponse report_simplified_invoice(invoice, pcsid, clearance_status, accept_language=None) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, optional language ValidationResponse clear_standard_invoice(invoice, pcsid, clearance_status, accept_language=None) SignedInvoice, CsidProduction, Boolean, optional language ValidationResponse

clearance_status is a required Boolean controlling the request header; use False for ordinary reporting and True for clearance. It does not describe the result. accept_language is a string or None controlling the language header. These methods do not expose an asynchronous or cancellation-token parameter.

A successful HTTP request does not guarantee acceptance. Call outcome() to obtain InvoiceOutcome, or ensure_accepted() to raise for rejected/unknown outcomes. cleared_invoice_xml() returns str | None; save that XML for an accepted clearance when present. reporting_status() and clearance_status() also return optional strings. See API request and response contracts and the API guide.
